title: Clowns Gambit
author: OpenToFriends
selftext:
Clown's Gambit is chess with the lights off. You can only see the squares your pieces can see. Everything else is fog, and the other player's pieces are somewhere in it.  
  
There is no check and no checkmate. If you can take the king, you win. If you leave yours sitting there, that's on you.  
  
What's different from normal chess:  
  
Random armies. Both kings start on e1 and e8. Every other piece is drawn at random from pawns, knights, bishops, rooks and queens, separately for each side. You can open with three queens. So can they. (Practice has a Classic option if you just want the normal line-up.)  
  
Fog. A rook sees down its lines, a knight sees where it can jump, a pawn sees the squares in front of it. Anything outside that is black. Enemy pieces and the board's tricks stay hidden until one of your pieces can see them.  
  
Trick tiles. Sixteen squares in the middle of the board do something when a piece lands on them: Snare, Binding, Taffy Floor, Marionette Strings, Moon Boots, Confetti Cannon, Lantern. Two of them are secret and carry no marker at all. The first piece to land on one finds out what it does.  
  
Two cards, one use each. Searchlight lights up a 3x3 patch of the board for a turn and a bit. Stage Swap trades the places of two of your pieces that sit next to each other. Using a card takes your whole turn.  
  
Short clocks. Casual games are 5 minutes each plus 3 seconds a move.  
  
Ways to play:  
Learn to play is a set of short lessons on the rules.  
Practice is a game against the Clockwork Clown bot. Gentle leaves you openings to learn from. Standard takes anything you give it. Nothing is rated.  
Play a friend makes a private, unrated game and a link you can send someone.  
Play casual matches you with another person online.  
Play ranked needs an account with a verified email. There's a leaderboard and a match history you can replay.  
Everything except ranked works as a guest, no sign-up. Pick a piece, pick a square, press confirm. A keyboard works too.  
  
A few things worth knowing:  
  
Online matching only works if somebody else is online at the same moment, and right now that may be nobody. The bot and friend games don't depend on that. If you want a game, say so in the comments and give a time.  
  
It's built for phones held upright and for desktop. The 3D board switches itself to a flat 2D board if your device struggles. I haven't been able to test on many different phones, so if something breaks on yours, tell me which phone and browser.  
  
In-game chat has report, mute and block buttons.  
  
The game runs on its own server, so it needs an internet connection.  
  
The pictures, the card art and the 3D pieces were made with AI image and 3D tools.
